children: Japanese rubber futures edged lower on Wednesday, as pressure from a stronger yen offset signs of tightening Indonesian supply and a rally in oil prices.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 1 yen, or 0.23%, at 437.6 yen ($2.85) per kg as of 0205 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 145 yuan, or 0.74%, to 19,610 yuan ($2,923.07) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 350 yuan, or 2.24%, to 15,990 yuan per metric ton.

steadied near its strongest level since February, keeping the dollar on the defensive as traders grappled with oil prices pushing towards $100 per barrel in the face of a widening war in the Middle East.
A stronger currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers.
Indonesia's exports of natural rubber were down 21% year-on-year at 765,000 tons in the first seven months of 2026, according to rubber information provider Qinrex.
The decline reinforces concerns over supply tightness in one of the top rubber producers and adds to the potential impact of El Niño in the coming months, a Singapore-based trader said.
Prices are further supported by expectations of tighter Indonesian supply due to ongoing haze and forest fires, the trader added.

Oil prices jumped for a fourth consecutive session, gaining more than $1 in early trade on Wednesday after Iran launched fresh attacks on U.S. military assets in the Gulf as the war between Washington and Tehran continued to spill out across the region.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded flat at 247.7 U.S. cents per kg.
